subject: LedgeCraft: compliance acceptance checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@ledgecraft.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@ledgecraft.com>
Cc: LedgerCraft Security <security@ledgecraft.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: LedgeCraft: compliance acceptance checklist & next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the candid run-through. Short recap from our side and explicit next steps so we can keep momentum toward technical acceptance.

Highlights from the call (pain / priority):
- Audit log & retention: you need immutable audit logs retained for 3 years for transaction tracing and regulatory review. Redwood default retention window is 90 days; you indicated any roadmap to 3 years would need to be operationalized via archive exports and a DPA appendix.
- SOC 2 attestation: LedgeCraft requires SOC 2 Type II evidence for the last 12 months. You want a summary pack and the auditor contact in case of cross-checking timelines.
- Pen test artifacts: request for latest penetration test report, scope, and remediation timeline.
- Data-flow mapping: you asked for a simple mapping of where PII and payment tokens touch Redwood (prefixes, KV cache behavior, and optional on-prem connector).
- SLA / retention exception: retention >1 year may trigger contract addendum and price delta.

Owners & immediate asks (who does what, by when):
1) Redwood — Vanessa: send SOC 2 summary + retention mapping template (attached). Deliverable: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, retention-mapping-template.xlsx. ETA: Thu 2026-08-27 EOD.
2) LedgeCraft — Rajiv: confirm the canonical list of data classes you need retained and whether archiving to S3 (customer-managed) is acceptable. ETA: Mon 2026-08-30.
3) Redwood Legal — Irene: draft DPA appendix options and a sample language snippet for a retention addendum and pen-test evidence sharing. ETA: Fri 2026-09-03.
4) Redwood Security — Ben (we'll loop him into any technical evidence requests and pen-test scoping). Ben will also surface any platform constraints for immutable 3-year audit logs.

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute technical handoff (security + infra) — Tue 2026-08-31 10:30am PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda: 1) retention architecture, 2) SOC2 evidence packet walk-through, 3) pen-test scope/ownership.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary of controls + auditor), retention-mapping-template.xlsx (simple table for your data classes), dpa-diff-highlight.docx (sample redlines we typically see).

If I missed anything from your side, call it out and I’ll update.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: LedgeCraft: compliance acceptance checklist & next steps

Thanks Vanessa — useful recap. Quick answers from our side:
- Retention: three years is preferred. Archiving to our S3 is acceptable provided logs are exported in a tamper-evident format (we can share required manifest schema).
- SOC 2: we need the auditor name and the last report period; we’ll pass any questions to our auditor if needed.
- Pen test: we’ll need scope (external/internal), and whether Redwood can provide copies of remediation notes.

We’d like the technical handoff on Tue 8/31; 10:30am PT works for Samantha and me.

Action for us: I’ll fill the retention-mapping-template and return by Mon 8/30. Also copying our security mailbox for any technical follow-ups.

—Rajiv

Looping in a quick note from infra/security:
- Immutable 3-year retention: technically we can support via WORM-style exports to a customer-managed S3 bucket; operationally this requires a runbook and a small engineering effort to add manifest signing to each export. Estimate: 2-3 sprints for implementation + QA. Potential cost: export & long-term storage billed to customer if they manage the S3 bucket.
- Pen test artifacts: we can share the last pen-test report (redacted in parts) and remediation summary; legal needs to confirm what can be shared verbatim.

Irene — can you start a DPA appendix draft focusing on retention addendum and evidence-sharing constraints? I’ll prepare a short tech appendix for the export format.

—Ben
